sessionTitle: Profile and optimize agentic AI on Windows

announcements.name: Time-correlated platform telemetry across IP blocks
announcements.shortDescription: Data from multiple drivers operating in different time domains is unified into one time domain, removing the burden of manual correlation previously required of tooling
announcements.longDescription: A capability called unified telemetry puts data from multiple drivers—which often operate in different time domains—into the same, time-correlated time domain. It collects platform telemetry from CPU, GPU, NPU, and power (and can incorporate OS-specific data via ETW), and combines it with application-side software tracing through ITT (Intel Instrumentation and Tracing Technology), an open-source project used to instrument much of the Intel AI stack such as OpenVINO and oneDNN [inferred]. Previously, getting data from different drivers at different rates and time domains required a tool chain to align them manually, which was always a complex problem; unified telemetry, available starting this week, removes that burden.

announcements.name: OpenVINO runtime fully instrumented for tracing
announcements.shortDescription: The OpenVINO runtime is fully instrumented with ITT markers, with additional layers such as Windows ML being added on top
announcements.longDescription: The OpenVINO runtime is fully instrumented with ITT tracing, and additional layers such as Windows ML are being added on top. Unified telemetry combines the software-side ITT tracing information with driver telemetry into a single, time-synchronized output, currently in JSON, with this being the first preview starting this week. Platform telemetry provides metrics such as memory reads/writes to DRAM, IP-block-to-IP-block bandwidth, power, and utilization, allowing AI model execution to be correlated with these metrics for optimization. Over time the output may gain a database—such as a columnar or vector database—to make queries more efficient.

announcements.name: JSON-based, AI-queryable trace output
announcements.shortDescription: Software traces are organized into structured domains (for example "OV phases") so AI models can be queried to generate breakdowns and reports
announcements.longDescription: Software traces, which are generally unstructured, are organized into structured domains so AI models can be run against them to produce analysis. In OpenVINO, the top-level layer captures the phases of execution under the "OV phases" domain name, so even with JSON output an AI model can be asked to look at the OV phases domain and generate a report and breakdown of the top level, then drill deeper. The goal is to organize software traces so they become friendly for AI and for future queries, enabling metrics like time to first token and decoding rate to be computed and then explored at operator or layer-level detail.
